definitions.explanation: A person who watches an event, performance, or unusual scene, typically out of curiosity rather than as a participant.

examples.japanese: {見物人|けんぶつにん}が{集|あつ}まる。
{火事|かじ}{現場|げんば}に{見物人|けんぶつにん}が{大勢|おおぜい}いた。
examples.english: There were many onlookers at the fire scene.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{行列|ぎょうれつ}を{見物人|けんぶつにん}が{道|みち}の{両側|りょうがわ}から{眺|なが}めていた。
examples.english: Spectators watched the festival procession from both sides of the street.

notes:
Composed of {見物|けんぶつ} (watching, sightseeing) + {人|にん} (person). Refers to someone watching an event or spectacle, often as a casual or curious bystander rather than an invited guest.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見物人|けんぶつにん}が{集|あつ}まる: onlookers gather
- {大勢|おおぜい}の{見物人|けんぶつにん}: a large crowd of spectators
- {見物人|けんぶつにん}でにぎわう: to be lively with spectators

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {観客|かんきゃく}: audience — people who attend a performance or game, often with tickets
- {野次馬|やじうま}: rubberneckers — onlookers who gather purely out of idle curiosity, with a negative nuance
